newsitem.title: USA: Oklahoma bomb jury deliberates McVeigh sentence.
newsitem.headline: Oklahoma bomb jury deliberates McVeigh sentence.

text.p: A jury on Thursday began deliberating whether Timothy McVeigh should be executed or spend life in prison for the Oklahoma City bombing, in which 168 people died.

The jury heard six days of testimony in the sentencing phase of the trial, after McVeigh was convicted on June 2 of the April 19, 1995 bombing of the Alfred P. Murrah federal building. More than 500 people were also injured in the attack.

The prosecution presented testimony from dozens of survivors and victims' relatives who described the devastating impact of the crime on their lives. Prosecutors say McVeigh bombed the building to avenge what he saw as grave abuses of power by the federal government.
In their effort to save McVeigh's life, defense attorneys tried to explain his anger over government actions and called his mother, father and old friends to plead for him.
The seven men and five women of the jury must decide unanimously whether McVeigh should be executed or spend his life in prison without the possibility of parole.
Whatever the jury's decision, Oklahoma authorities have said they also want to try him on state murder charges.
